description: Tracks Leather net balance over a 40-hour balanced playstyle session. Supply comes from armor salvage (primary), common-materials loot rolls, and biome-plains/biome-forest loot rolls. Demand comes from armor recipes (Leather Armor, Leather Cap, Leather Boots, Leather Leggings, Leather Gloves, Reinforced Leather, mixed weapon/armor recipes requiring Leather as a binding) and the Tannery construction cost.

armorSalvage.comment: Post-tune: BuildArmorYields base 3, clamped [3,6], avg ~4 with bonus from workmanship/skill.

commonMaterialsLoot.comment: common-materials pool has 6 equal-weight entries, one of which is Leather.

biomePlainsLoot.comment: Post-tune: Leather added to biome-plains with weight 2 of 7 total.

biomeForestLoot.comment: Post-tune: Leather added to biome-forest with weight 2 of 7 total.

preTuneSnapshot.comment: Tight break-even on paper but in practice -1/hour due to armor drops often being W1 (yielding only 2-3 leather) + Tannery burning 5 upfront + leather-heavy recipe bursts. Matches user playtest feedback: 'leather qtys are very low'.

postTuneSnapshot.comment: Tune applied: (1) BuildArmorYields base 2 → 3, clamp [3,6]; (2) Leather added to biome-plains (weight 2); (3) Leather added to biome-forest (weight 2). Result: +~7/hour leather supply, net +6/hour — comfortably above break-even without flooding.

designIntent: Leather should be a mild bottleneck that the player actively manages, not a chronic drag. A small sustained surplus (+5-10/hour) is the design target: it encourages players to explore plains/forest biomes and rewards salvage habit, without making Leather feel worthless.
